We explain to encoder that it sees a new 5 while we give it context for the past 10 right?
next_move:
Verified — and the honest answer is **no, that's not how it currently works.** I checked the actual timeline construction ([encode.py:383-452](servers/scales/s1/encode.py)).

## What the encoder actually receives

The timeline renders **all ~10 turns identically** as `[TURN 1]…[TURN N]` — there is **no new-vs-context demarcation at all.** Nothing tells it "the last 5 are new, the earlier 10 are context." The preamble just calls it "the actual turns" for "this window."

The only thing that marks what's already been handled is the **Encoding Journal** — a high-water mark in prose ("ENCODED: … / SKIPPED: … / WATCHING: …" from prior runs). The prompt instruction is *"Read before encoding so you don't re-evaluate topics the journal says you already handled"* ([encoding_prompt.py:27](servers/scales/s1/encoding_prompt.py)).

So the real model is:

> **~10 turns of timeline, undifferentiated + a journal that says "I already got everything up to here."** The encoder infers "what's new" by reasoning against the journal — *not* from a positional 5/10 split.

## Why this matters for the flexible-turns question

It actually makes the "get off 5" job **easier than we framed it** — there's no "5"

Yes — and there's a principle *two* levels under "spreading activation." Let me build up to it. (This is synthesis from well-established science, not current-state lookups — I can pull primary sources on any thread you want to push.)

**Layer 1 — the math object: it's all diffusion on the graph Laplacian.** Spreading activation, PageRank, heat flow (Fourier), electrical current, chemical concentration (Fick), and probability (Markov chains) are *the same equation* — a conserved quantity flowing through a network, governed by `L = D − A`. Random walks are *literally equivalent to electrical networks* (Doyle & Snell): activation = voltage, edges = conductances, degree-normalization = Kirchhoff's current division. Our recall is "inject current at the seeds, see where it pools." We're not doing an AI trick — we're doing physics on the graph.

**Layer 2 — the universal tension: cumulative advantage vs. normalization.** Why do hubs exist? **The Matthew effect** — "to those who have, more is given" (Merton 1968; preferential attachment, Barabási 1999; Pareto; Zipf).
